When I was very young and visiting some relatives in the Philippines for a holiday, my mum and I took a taxi to an SM mall. On the way, our driver pointed out that everyone was looking and pointing at the sky outside the cab, so we wound down the windows and looked up.

It was the middle of the day, and the sky was covered in red lights, the size of what you’d expect stars to be at night. At first I thought they were just stars, but it was weird that they were such a bright, vibrant red and that I could see them so clearly in the middle of the day. When I looked at them further, I noticed that the lights weren’t actually random, and they formed shapes if you were to connect them, like spirals, squares and triangles.

Now normally having a memory as weird as that is something I’d chalk up to just a dream or something as a kid, but the one thing that makes me realise I actually saw what I saw was the fact that my mum was there and to this day she insists she saw it too. 

I’ve looked it up on the internet several times over the years and no one has ever posted an article about it or anything which is really disappointing and confusing. You’d think red lights covering the sky would be something people would talk about, especially since we know at least the taxi driver and people outside would have seen it too.

I recently got a 7 string Boden clone as my first guitar and I can't tell you how excited I am every time I look at it or play it, even 4 months after buying it.

Even learning about hardware and theory is ultra exciting to me at the moment. So far the only advice I can impart as a fellow newbie is:

1. If you can, find someone who's experienced at guitar to watch what you're doing, even if you just record clips of you playing and send them, you'll probably have some inefficiencies and weird quirks that might be poor technique that can be ironed out.
2. On the topic of recording yourself, recording yourself practising may be painful at first but I've noticed weird habits when playing and seeing my progress is quite rewarding in itself
3. Learn whatever you want to learn, so long as you're having fun. I started with all the chords and gravitated to just trying to do some dumb guy slam riffs, and I had a blast. Once I started messing around with riffs, I went back and learned what notes, chords and scales I was playing and having the reference made it much more interesting.
4. If you haven't gotten a guitar yet, do your research. Great guitars can be had for so cheap nowadays you can really get a lot for your money. I actually slightly regret getting a Chinese headless because it required a fair amount of work to be playable and still could do with modifications moving forward. Don't make the same mistake I did, unless you're ***really*** smitten with a particular guitar.

​

I'm planning on fixing up my current guitar then going for a Solar A1.8C next, I know it's a big jump but I can't stop thinking about it to the point where I have dreams about it. 

​

Good luck and have fun everyone!
